what_its_for: Mexiletine is used to treat certain types of irregular heartbeats (called arrhythmias). It works by slowing down electrical signals in the heart to help keep your heart beating in a normal, steady rhythm. It is also sometimes used off-label to treat certain types of muscle stiffness (myotonia) and nerve pain.
how_to_take: Take mexiletine exactly as your doctor tells you. Always take it with food, milk, or antacids to help reduce stomach upset. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the capsule. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady amount in your body.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how well your heart responds and how well you tolerate the medicine. A common starting dose is 200 mg taken every 8 hours (3 times a day). Your doctor may adjust your dose up to 400 mg every 8 hours if needed. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it is within 4 hours of when you were supposed to take it. If more than 4 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mexiletine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid caffeine and caffeine-containing products (like coffee, tea, energy drinks, and some sodas) as they may increase side effects such as shakiness or a fast heartbeat. Avoid smoking, as it can lower the effectiveness of this medicine. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how mexiletine affects you, since it can cause dizziness or blurred vision. Avoid alcohol, as it may worsen dizziness. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, as many drugs can interact with mexiletine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a new or worsening irregular heartbeat or fast/slow/pounding heartbeat, chest pain or pressure, severe dizziness or fainting, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, severe nausea or vomiting, uncontrollable shaking or tremors, confusion or unusual mood changes, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing.
when_it_works: Mexiletine starts working within a few hours of your first dose. However, it may take several days to a few weeks before your heart rhythm is fully stable and your doctor can find the best dose for you. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better, as stopping suddenly can be dangerous.
special_populations: Older adults (seniors): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, so use with extra caution and follow your doctor's dosing instructions carefully. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking mexiletine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the risks and benefits need to be carefully weighed. Breastfeeding: Mexiletine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. Liver disease: If you have liver problems, your doctor may need to lower your dose, as your body may process this drug more slowly. Kidney disease: Dose adjustments are generally not needed, but tell your doctor about any kidney problems you have.
